A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DIFFEOCFM and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched despite reformatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation-quality and downstream-classification results on five neuroimaging datasets, alongside computational and neurophysiological analyses.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, including additional RIEMCFM comparisons, runtime measurements, and architecture ablations.

M1.justification: The pullback-CFM formulation, embeddings, objectives, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. However, the reported numerical sampling procedure changes from midpoint integration with step size 10^-3 in v1 Appendix J to dopri5 in v2 Section 4.3, constituting a limited inference-procedure revision.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ABIDE, ADNI, OASIS-3, BNCI2014-002, and BNCI2015-001, retaining the same disease-classification and motor-imagery tasks and simulated-SPD scalability study. The new architecture experiments use the existing ABIDE coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds affine-invariant RIEMCFM to both EEG comparisons in Table 1, providing an important direct manifold-based comparator. v1 discussed Riemannian CFM but excluded it as inapplicable. Existing comparators, including the separate SPD-DDPM timing comparison, are retained.

E3.justification: The reported integration setting changes from fixed-step midpoint to dopri5. Added experiments specify RIEMCFM's six-layer network and learning rate, and ABIDE sweeps over widths 8–1024 and one to four hidden layers. Figure 3 additionally summarizes performance through an average of quality F1 and CAS F1. These are bounded extensions within the retained evaluation framework.

E4.justification: New Appendix K systematically tests sensitivity to network width and depth, reporting quality and computational costs in Tables 3–4. This adds substantive evidence for the chosen shallow, 512-unit architecture that v1 lacked. Existing projection, constraint-satisfaction, and neurophysiological analyses are largely retained.

E5.justification: v2 increases the reported fMRI repetitions from five to ten subject-grouped splits and newly explains EEG standard deviations as computed over five inner splits and averaged over sessions. Table 1 adds one-sided paired Wilcoxon tests at alpha = 0.05, replacing bolding of numerical winners with significance-aware comparisons. Mean and standard-deviation reporting already existed in v1.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds RIEMCFM outcomes and training/sampling times, while Tables 3–4 add architecture-sensitivity results. Existing scores also change: DIFFEOCFM's ADNI CAS F1 is 0.35 ± 0.09 in v1 and 0.47 ± 0.10 in v2. These are revised results under changed reported settings, not an established same-setting gain. The OASIS-3 connectome panel is also replaced.

T1.justification: Propositions 1–3 and their proofs remain substantively identical, as do the pullback identities, affine-invariant quotient geometry, and projection derivation. Discussion of alternative embeddings and dimensionality limitations does not introduce a new formal result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: exact reformulation of pullback Riemannian CFM in Euclidean coordinates, efficient manifold-valid generation, and realistic brain-connectivity synthesis for both covariance and correlation matrices. Added evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: Section 6 adds uncertainty about alternative connectivity estimators, including partial correlations and graphical-Lasso precision, and strengthens the dimensionality limitation to exponential sample-complexity growth. Section 3.2 also explains the embeddings' selection for simplicity and identifies alternatives. These refine applicability and interpretation without changing the central conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 adds project-code and implementation links, RIEMCFM configuration details, and the One-Class SVM explanation for the already-used EvaGeM evaluator. Most existing training and hardware details move into Section 4.3. Conversely, v1's explicit affine-invariant tangent-space preprocessing description for CAS is omitted; this does not establish that the preprocessing itself changed.

R1.justification: Related work adds connections to Lie-group reparameterization, manifold diffusion processes, and metric flow matching, including acknowledgment of an earlier precursor. The baseline discussion corrects v1's characterization of Riemannian CFM as inapplicable, recognizing its usable but costlier SPD implementation. The overall novelty positioning remains intact.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence are largely retained. Changes include localized explanatory additions, moving implementation details into the main text, reorganizing appendices, revising the conclusion heading, and appending a NeurIPS checklist. These do not amount to a broad scientific rewrite.

P2.justification: Table 1 is substantially redesigned with runtime columns, RIEMCFM rows, highlighted DIFFEOCFM rows, and revised bolding. v2 adds the performance-versus-cost Figure 3 and two ablation tables, and adopts NeurIPS formatting throughout. Figure 9b replaces v1 Figure 8b's duplicated ABIDE imagery with a distinct OASIS-3 panel; most other figures are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: The direct RIEMCFM comparison resolves an important baseline gap in v1 and substantially strengthens evidence for the central efficiency claim at similar EEG generation quality. Architecture ablations, explicit statistical comparisons, and the corrected OASIS-3 figure further improve empirical credibility. Some claims remain poorly reconciled with the revised results: Section 5.1 still asserts universally highest CAS scores despite counterexamples in Table 1, and the CAS preprocessing description loses detail. These shortcomings do not outweigh the substantial improvement in comparative evidence.
